assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, insulinotropic activity of the processed peptide, and its pancreatic and central effects) led to GLP-1 receptor agonists that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiometabolic outcomes. The discovery is original, mechanistically clear and has unusually large, lasting impact on patients and on physiology of appetite and glucose control.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 biology, secretion and physiological actions over decades; Mojsov's early identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form is a key, partly contested piece. Knudsen's pharmaceutical design of long-acting analogues is a translational contribution that could be rewarded separately. Habener, who is not in the supplied credit list, may be seen as a comparable contributor, and I cannot fully adjudicate the competing priority claims from memory.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy and safety are confirmed by many large independent randomized trials and by real-world use; the field is mature, and timing is highly favourable given the clinical impact.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener-group work, Holst and Drucker is disputed and not resolvable from the supplied credit list.
Whether the committee would prefer to recognise pharmaceutical development (Knudsen) rather than a third basic scientist.
Long-term safety and durability of the obesity indications are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis, and that blocking it in patients produces major clinical benefit, established cytokine-targeted therapy for chronic inflammatory disease and changed outcomes in RA, IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. The concept-to-clinic path is exceptionally clear and the impact on autoimmune and inflammatory medicine is profound.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the key mechanistic work in human RA synovial cultures and the first clinical trials of anti-TNF antibody; this is a compact, defensible two-person configuration. Other contributors to TNF biology and antibody engineering (e.g. those who cloned or characterised TNF, or developed the antibodies) are outside the supplied list and could complicate allocation.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent clinical evidence and widespread long-term use; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the underlying TNF discovery and for antibody engineering falls outside the supplied names.
Whether the committee regards this as clinical-translational work suited to the prize relative to purely basic discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, opening a new modality of living drugs. The conceptual and clinical advance is major and still expanding to other diseases, including autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation with CD19 CAR-T), Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulated CARs and preclinical proof) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells) are plausible; the foundational chimeric-receptor concept (Eshhar and others) is not on the supplied list, and early CAR design contributors are numerous.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent trials confirm efficacy in B-cell malignancies; limitations in solid tumours, toxicity and cost remain, but the core principle is mature.
uncertainties: Foundational priority of the chimeric receptor concept and which of the three best represents the decisive contribution.
Durability beyond a decade and secondary malignancy concerns are still being assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method to control defined cell populations with millisecond precision using light-gated channels, and has transformed neuroscience and, increasingly, cardiac and retinal research. The invention is original, widely adopted and has been clinically applied in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: The channelrhodopsin characterization by Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann and the neuronal implementation by Deisseroth and Boyden, with Miesenböck's earlier genetic photostimulation, make a six-name credit list that exceeds the three-laureate limit; any trio leaves out decisive contributors, which is a major unresolved allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Technology is confirmed in thousands of labs over two decades; therapeutic use is early but the research impact is mature.
uncertainties: Three-person limit versus at least five to six credible contributors.
Relative weight of the tool development versus the later discoveries it enabled, and of Bamberg versus Nagel and Hegemann.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers, with population-level evidence of strongly reduced precancer and cancer incidence. The discovery is a clean, high-impact example of cancer prevention by vaccination.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach, while Frazer and colleagues in Australia contributed the VLP vaccine technology; priority between groups (including Zhou and others) is contested and not fully captured by the supplied names. The earlier prize for HPV as a cause of cervical cancer (2008) is a separate matter.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent epidemiological confirmation from national vaccination programmes; cancer-incidence reductions are now being documented, so timing is good.
uncertainties: Priority dispute with other VLP developers outside the supplied credit list.
Overlap with the zur Hausen recognition may lead the committee to consider the vaccine less novel.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that BCL-2 acts as a survival rather than proliferation gene established the genetic control of apoptosis in cancer and led to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax for CLL and other leukemias. The discovery has a clear lineage from fundamental cell-death biology to approved therapy.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams characterized the Bcl-2 gene family and its role in lymphoma; Vaux showed in the context of cell-death regulation that BCL-2 blocks death; Strasser is a major contributor. The mechanistic link to the C. elegans cell-death work previously recognised and the contributions of Korsmeyer and others outside the list complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed widely across tumour types with approved drugs; interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Role of the earlier translocation discovery (Tsujimoto and others) and Korsmeyer, who is deceased, outside the list.
Selecting three among four credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified cytosolic DNA as a danger signal for innate immunity and linked it to antiviral defence, autoimmunity (such as interferonopathies and lupus-related inflammation) and cancer immunity. It is conceptually important and generated a large field, though from my perspective in autoimmunity the clinical translation is still developing.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAMP and cGAS as the DNA sensor; Barber and Ishikawa identified STING as the adaptor. Sun and Wu were co-discoverers in Chen's group, so the credit list is broad and a three-person limit is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is robustly confirmed, but therapeutic validation, including STING agonists and inhibitors, is not yet established.
uncertainties: Allocation among Chen's co-workers, Barber and Ishikawa, and whether STING or cGAS carries the key discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning and characterization of IL-6 and its receptor, followed by IL-6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab, define a cytokine-targeted therapy used in rheumatoid arthritis, giant cell arteritis, cytokine release syndrome and other conditions. It is a clear case of molecular discovery leading to treatment of immune-mediated disease.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano are the central figures in the cloning of IL-6 (as B-cell stimulatory factor 2) and its biology; the credit list is compact. Contributions from other groups to the parallel identification of the molecule are not captured and could be questioned.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent trials and long-term clinical use confirm benefit; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Relative priority of parallel discoveries of the same cytokine by other groups.
Whether its therapeutic impact is judged to outrank anti-TNF in the same field, which I see as the stronger case.
